body:
# Independent audit: a genuine critical circuit with individual potential efficiency below Gamma



The only non-elementary input below is the classical ordinary Grünbaum centroid inequality. The facet convex-order inequality used for the potential upper bound is already fully proved in `candidate 8e69e6820cd6ee00` and independently audited in `historical context (not an accepted premise)`.

## 1. Exact lattice and measure

Fix `d>=2` and set `n=d`, `m=d+1`. Let

    v0=(-1,...,-1), vi=e_i for 1<=i<=d,
    P={0,v0,...,vd}, D=conv(v0,...,vd).

The vertices are affinely independent: their difference matrix is `I+11^T`, whose determinant is `d+1`. Thus `D` is full-dimensional. Define

    ell0(z)=-sum z_i,
    elli(z)=(d+1)z_i-sum z_j, 1<=i<=d.

Then `sum ell_j=0`, and `ell_j(v_j)=d`, `ell_j(v_k)=-1` for `k!=j`. The barycentric coordinates of `D` are `(ell_j+1)/(d+1)`, so

    D={ell_j>=-1 for every j}.

To verify **all** lattice points, put `s=sum z_i` for an integer `z in D`. The inequalities imply `-d<=s<=1` and `z_i>=(s-1)/(d+1)`. If `s=-d`, every `z_i>=-1`, and their sum forces `z=v0`. If `-d<s<=0`, integrality forces every `z_i>=0`, hence `s=0,z=0`. If `s=1`, the nonnegative integer coordinates give one of the `e_i`. Therefore

    D intersect Z^d=P.

Let `K` be any full-dimensional `d`-simplex, with volume `V>0`, barycentric coordinates `lambda_0,...,lambda_d`, and centroid `g`. The actual ambient convex body is

    C=D times K.

It has exactly the indicated `d+2` positive integer fibers, all equal to `K`. Hence `q=d`, `H_d(S)=(d+2)V`, and every fiber-sum identity is the ordinary additivity of Hausdorff measure on finitely many disjoint parallel `d`-planes.

## 2. Genuine regular global critical caps

Define the closed ambient halfspaces

    H_j={lambda_j(x)-1/m+ell_j(z)>=0}.

At base zero, this is the canonical simplex vertex cap through `g`, of volume `Gamma_d V`, where `Gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d`. At `v_j` the minimum margin is `d-1/m>0`, so the entire fiber is strictly captured. At any other `v_k` the maximum margin is `-1/m<0`, so the entire fiber is strictly missed. Therefore every cap has the same raw mass

    Q=(1+Gamma_d)V.                                  (1)

Their affine margins sum to zero everywhere in the full ambient space. Thus they cover that space and give `D_S(Y)<=Q` for every actual point `Y`.

For the lower bound at `Y0=(0,g)`, let a closed ambient halfspace be

    H={a.z+u.x>=b}, with u.g>=b.

For a uniform random point `X` of `K`, let `X_0,...,X_d` be its cyclic barycentric permutations. Each is uniform in `K`, and pointwise

    sum_j X_j=m g, sum_j v_j=0.

Consequently the `m` margins `a.v_j+u.X_j-b` have nonnegative sum. At least one is nonnegative for every sample, including equality samples. Integration gives

    sum_j |K intersect H_(v_j)|>=V.                 (2)

The middle fiber contributes at least `Gamma_d V` by ordinary Grünbaum; when `u=0`, it contributes its entire volume, so the same inequality holds. Equations (1)--(2) prove that the global maximum raw depth is exactly `Q`, attained at `Y0`, for all ambient oblique, vertical and closed halfspaces.

Only the middle fibers have nonzero sections for the displayed caps. The canonical section centroid is `g`: its fixed coordinate is `1/m`, and its other barycentric coordinates at its centroid are also `1/m`. Its coarea mass is

    sigma_j=d (d/(d+1))^(d-1) V,

because `lambda_j` has density `d(1-t)^(d-1)` under uniform volume. Thus all coarea masses agree, independently of the affine shape of `K`. The full mixed section centroid is `(0,g)` for every cap. The full ambient normals sum to zero, and positive circuit weights can all equal one; the corresponding normalized response weights are exactly `theta_j=1/m`.

The middle cuts are proper; all other traces are strictly empty or strictly full. A proper section meets the middle fiber boundary in surface measure zero. Hence the circuit is regular and carries no nonsmooth supporting-face allocation issue.

## 3. The deepest point is unique

Every outer base is exposed in `conv P`, so its mixed depth equals its ordinary fiber depth and is at most `V/2<Q`. This also follows directly by adding a sufficiently large exposing tilt to an ordinary cap.

If `x!=g` in the middle simplex, at least one `lambda_j(x)>1/m`. The shifted ambient cap

    {lambda_j(w)+ell_j(z)>=lambda_j(x)}

contains `(0,x)`, still strictly captures the whole `v_j` fiber, and strictly misses every other outer fiber. Its middle volume is `(1-lambda_j(x))^d V<Gamma_d V`. Its total is therefore strictly smaller than `Q`. The unique global deepest point is `(0,g)`.

## 4. Exact optimum over all convex normal-dependent potentials

On each outer normal bundle, the profile `W=m^(-1) sum 1_Hj` is the constant `1/m`. On the middle boundary it is the canonical simplex profile `W0`.

For a finite nonnegative potential `Phi(n,z,x)`, convex in `(z,x)` for each fixed normal, write

    I0=integral_(boundary K) Phi(n(x),0,x) dH_(d-1),
    Ij=integral_(boundary K) Phi(n(x),v_j,x) dH_(d-1),
    T=sum_j Ij.

All fibers are the same body, so their outward normals at a given boundary point agree. Jensen's inequality at `0=m^(-1)sum v_j` holds pointwise at this *same* `x` and normal, giving

    I0<=T/m.                                         (3)

The proved simplex-facet convex order, applied separately on every facet to the restriction of `Phi` at base zero, gives

    integral_(boundary K) Phi(n(x),0,x) W0(x) <=Gamma_d I0.  (4)

Thus the full efficiency satisfies

    integral Phi W / integral Phi
       <=[Gamma_d I0+T/m]/[I0+T].                   (5)

For a positive denominator, (3) forces `T>0`. Since `Gamma_d>1/m` for `d>=2`, the right side of (5) increases with `I0/T` and is at most

    (1+Gamma_d)/(d+2).                              (6)

The strict inequality `Gamma_d>1/(d+1)` is the strict Bernoulli inequality
`(1-1/(d+1))^d>1-d/(d+1)` for `d>=2`.

The constant potential `Phi=1` attains (6). Indeed `I0` and every `Ij` are the same surface area. On each middle facet the mean of `W0` is `Gamma_d`: its `d` nonempty cap pieces each occupy the relative fraction `(d/(d+1))^(d-1)`, and each has weight `1/(d+1)`. Consequently

    sup efficiency=(1+Gamma_d)/(d+2)<Gamma_d.         (7)

This is an upper bound for the entire indicated potential cone, not merely a finite set of test functions or normal-only multipliers.

For `d=2`, the values are `Gamma_2=4/9` and exact optimum/global normalized depth `13/36`, with gap `1/12` below `Gamma_2`.

## 5. Exact limitations and quota-aware variants

The `d+2` bases have distinct parity classes when `d>=2`: `0`, the `d` coordinate unit vectors, and the all-one parity vector of `v0`. Thus `k(P)=|P|=d+2`. With equal volumes, every subset has mass fraction `|T|/(d+2)=k(T)/k(P)`. In particular every nonempty proper closed minor has equality, rather than the strict quota required at a minimal bad family.

More strongly, **no choice of positive volumes on this same base** can satisfy all strict singleton quotas `w_z<1/k(P)`: there are exactly `k(P)` singletons and their normalized masses sum to one. Each outer vertex is also parity-unique. Therefore this construction does not test a quota-conditioned individual-efficiency claim.

It is not an OC counterexample. Already any ordinary fiber centroid captures at least `Gamma_d V` from its own fiber, which pays the OC target because `d+2<=2^d` for `d>=2`. The latter inequality is equality at `d=2`, and follows inductively thereafter. The actual global depth (1) is much larger.

The example shows that lattice completeness, a single deterministic unique deepest center, regularity, equal global cap masses, balanced full ambient normals, and exact mixed section centroids do **not** by themselves imply individual `Gamma_d` efficiency. A surviving variant must retain an additional premise such as the minimal-bad-family quotas, a small global depth hypothesis, or another genuine geometric restriction. No such strengthened implication is proved here.

## 6. Full source reconciliation and exact verification

I independently read the final root source `candidate d7fcf9727e1fd83d`. Its geometric, measure, criticality, full-cone and scope claims all pass. Its repeated symbol `I_0` for a central and an outer integral is explicitly disambiguated by the subsequent name `A`; using different names from the outset would improve notation but does not change the argument. Its alternative Bernoulli estimate `Gamma_d>=2d/(d+1)^2>1/(d+1)` is also correct.

The independent verifier `supporting computation verify_lattice_simplex_critical_profile_obstruction_slab_recovery.py` passes **1,350 exact checks**: bounded lattice enumeration, determinant and parity certificates, actual canonical simplex cap determinants and section centroids, strict full/empty trace inequalities, exact cyclic transport marginals/averages, closed-halfspace nonnegative-sum checks, and the profile-envelope identity. The proof above, rather than finite enumeration, supplies arbitrary dimension.

For clarity, if `r=I0/T`, the exact upper-envelope gap is

    beta-(Gamma_d r+1/m)/(1+r)
      =(m Gamma_d-1)(1-m r)/[m(m+1)(1+r)]>=0.

This explicitly includes `I0=0` and equality at `I0=T/m`; no limiting or unattained optimization is used.
